knowledge:
- key_parameters: prior_param=List of hyperparameters (alpha, mu0, s0, a0, b0) for the Dirichlet Process mixture model, which are robust to many settings ;; testZeroes=Logical indicating whether to perform a chi-squared test for differences in dropout rate (differential zeroes, DZ) ;; permutations=Integer specifying the number of permutations for the Bayes Factor test; if set to 0 (default), the fast Kolmogorov-Smirnov test is used instead ;; categorize=Logical; if set to FALSE, skips the classification of genes into DD patterns for faster computation ;; condition=Character specifying the colData column name containing biological condition labels (defaults to 'condition') ;; zero.thresh=Numeric threshold in preprocess to filter out genes with a high proportion of zeroes (e.g., 0.9 for 90%) ;; scran_norm=Logical; if TRUE in preprocess, applies scran normalization to the counts
- alternatives: The fast Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test is used by default (permutations=0) as a computationally efficient alternative to the full Bayes Factor permutation test. While KS has slightly lower power at lower sample sizes (50-75 cells per condition) primarily affecting DB pattern genes, it is orders of magnitude faster and does not require permutations.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing single-cell RNA-seq data to detect complex differences in gene expression distributions (such as changes in modality, proportion of cell subpopulations, or dropout rates) across two biological conditions, rather than just traditional mean shifts.
- pitfalls: Input data must be formatted as a SingleCellExperiment object and contain normalized counts (unless raw counts are preprocessed using the preprocess function). Genes with one or fewer nonzero measurements across all cells will not be tested for differential distribution of expressed measurements (though they can still be tested for DZ if testZeroes=TRUE). Running the full permutation test (permutations > 0) is computationally intensive and requires at least 1000 permutations in practice; parallel processing should be configured using the param argument. If preprocess is run with scran_norm=TRUE on an object that already contains a normcounts assay, it will overwrite normcounts and move the original values to normcounts-orig.

workflows.name: differential_distribution_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify and classify differentially distributed genes between two biological conditions in single-cell RNA-seq data.
input: expression_matrix.csv (normalized or raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix)
metadata.csv (cell metadata containing biological condition labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct a SingleCellExperiment object from the expression matrices and condition labels ;; 2. Preprocess the data to filter out genes with high zero proportions and apply normalization ;; 3. Define the prior parameters for the mixture model ;; 4. Run the scDD engine to test for differential distributions and classify genes ;; 5. Extract the main results and partition estimates ;; 6. Visualize the expression distributions of significant genes using side-by-side violin plots
workflows.code:
condition <- c(rep(1, ncol(scDatExList$C1)), rep(2,  ncol(scDatExList$C2)))
names(condition) <- c(colnames(scDatExList$C1), colnames(scDatExList$C2))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays=list(normcounts=cbind(scDatExList$C1, scDatExList$C2)), colData=data.frame(condition))
scDatEx <- preprocess(scDatEx, zero.thresh=0.9)
scDatEx.scran <- preprocess(scDatEx, zero.thresh=0.5, scran_norm=TRUE)
prior_param=list(alpha=0.01, mu0=0, s0=0.01, a0=0.01, b0=0.01)
scDatExSim <- scDD(scDatExSim, prior_param=prior_param, testZeroes=FALSE)
RES <- results(scDatExSim)
PARTITION.C1 <- results(scDatExSim, type="Zhat.c1")
scDatExSim <- scDD(scDatExSim, prior_param=prior_param, testZeroes=FALSE, permutations=100)
de <- sideViolin(normcounts(scDatExSim)[1,], scDatExSim$condition, title.gene=rownames(scDatExSim)[1])
library(gridExtra)
grid.arrange(de, dp, dm, db, ep, ee, ncol=2)

workflows.name: single_cell_simulation
workflows.intent: Simulate a single-cell RNA-seq dataset with specified numbers of differentially distributed and equivalently distributed genes based on real pilot data.
input: pilot_data.rds (a SingleCellExperiment object containing real single-cell expression data to estimate simulation parameters)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the pilot SingleCellExperiment dataset ;; 2. Set simulation parameters including the number of genes for each pattern (DE, DP, DM, DB, EE, EP), sample size, and random seed ;; 3. Run simulateSet to generate the simulated dataset ;; 4. Extract the simulated expression values and true category/fold-change metadata
workflows.code:
data(scDatEx)
nDE <- 5
nDP <- 5
nDM <- 5
nDB <- 5
nEE <- 5
nEP <- 5
numSamples <- 100
seed <- 816
SD <- simulateSet(scDatEx, numSamples=numSamples, nDE=nDE, nDP=nDP, nDM=nDM, nDB=nDB, nEE=nEE, nEP=nEP, sd.range=c(2,2), modeFC=4, plots=FALSE, random.seed=seed)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
head(rowData(SD))
